stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and describes a complex live-preview feature across GO, UP, and MX. openspec must first elaborate requirements, define meaningful AC, and add technical depth for real-time preview behavior. speckit should then harden with testability criteria, security checks (XSS in preview rendering, auth for preview endpoints), and edge cases (network failures, concurrent edits, stale content).

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — no live preview support exists in the codebase. useContent is the single bottleneck (236+ callers) where preview mode awareness must attach. All Contentstack content resolution flows through this hook, so enabling preview there propagates to every consumer without touching individual components.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with a valuable note identifying useContent as the single bottleneck (236+ callers). I built the full AC set from scratch since none existed. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the core on/off behavior; (2) AC-3/AC-4 cover the real-time update lifecycle; (3) AC-5/AC-7/AC-11/AC-15 address error handling and edge cases (API failures, invalid tokens, rapid updates, partial content); (4) AC-6/AC-14 address security — preventing draft content from leaking via CDN cache or unauthorized access; (5) AC-8 ensures cross-site parity for GO/UP/MX; (6) AC-9 ensures nested/referenced content is also preview-aware (critical given ContentstackLink is a listed file); (7) AC-10 ensures zero regression in non-preview mode; (8) AC-12 prevents flash-of-published-content on SSR; (9) AC-13 adds a UX safeguard so editors don't confuse preview with live. I could not read the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, or ContentstackLink.tsx — if those files contain existing error boundaries, caching strategies, or SSR patterns, some ACs may need refinement to align with current architecture.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All three declared manifest paths (src/hooks/useContent.ts, src/interface/content/contentCard.ts, src/components/contentstack/ContentstackLink/ContentstackLink.tsx) are confirmed to exist with exact matches across all three codelines (gotransit, upexpress, metrolinx) — no missing or unresolved paths. Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified useContent as the single bottleneck (236+ callers) where preview-mode awareness must attach, giving the implementer a clear architectural anchor; speckit then built comprehensive coverage from scratch — security (XSS in preview rendering, unauthorized draft access, CDN cache leaks), error handling (API failures, invalid tokens, rapid updates), cross-site parity for GO/UP/MX, nested/referenced content preview-awareness, SSR flash-of-published-content prevention, and UX safeguards. The two roles are cleanly complementary. The three verificationCriteria present are all observable and testable (draft display without publish, real-time draft update without refresh, published-only fallback when preview inactive). The file set is plausible for a live-preview feature: useContent is the content-resolution hook, contentCard defines the content interface, and ContentstackLink handles nested content rendering. Minor open question: speckit's notes describe ~15 acceptance criteria covering security and edge cases, but only 3 verificationCriteria surfaced — the existing ones are testable but happy-path focused. This is an ordinary gap a competent writer resolves during implementation, not a blocking defect. Per brownfield policy, the empty acceptanceCriteria array and acceptanceChanged=false from both agents are expected and not penalized.
